claims.statement: California homeowners appetite guidance is internal carrier underwriting guidance for eligibility, evidence, referral, binding, and authority decisions; it must not be used to expand, restrict, waive, or interpret policy coverage, and a referral is not itself a declination, approval, coverage grant, or claim settlement position.

The California routine appetite positions Coverage A from $300,000 through $2,000,000 and protection class 7 or better, while the California Guide separately limits line binding authority to Coverage A not exceeding $1,000,000; appetite eligibility and delegated authority are separate gates.

Before binding, California underwriting must verify material occupancy, ownership, location, valuation, construction, protection, condition, coverage, and authority information, and must refer or decline when material facts are missing, conflicting, adverse, or unverifiable rather than relying on assumptions.

California roof controls combine two pre-bind gates: the California appetite Guide requires an acceptable roof inspection at roof age 20 years or greater, while the general Personal Lines Manual requires a roof survey when roof age reaches 15 years; active leakage, incomplete work, unresolved deterioration or repairs, inadequate or conflicting evidence, and inaccessible areas require decline, hold, referral, or an authorized exception rather than unsupported binding.

California wind and hail underwriting requires acceptable maintenance, verified mitigation evidence, and a wind mitigation inspection when Coverage A exceeds $1,000,000; prior unrepaired storm damage, vulnerable structures or equipment, recurring losses, and unsupported mitigation claims require referral, while deductible handling remains subject to approved authority.

California water-risk review begins with the physical water path and drainage arrangement, distinguishes sewer, drain, sump, envelope, surface-water, flood, seepage, and maintenance causes, and refers recurring backup, sump malfunction, unresolved drainage, unusual plumbing, or unsupported repair conditions; below-grade protections and requested backup limits require evidence and review.

The California Guide directs review of the preceding five years of loss history and referral when paid property claims reach two, with paid claims classified by property coverage and inquiries, unpaid reports, or withdrawn notices excluded unless payment is confirmed; cause, repairs, recurrence, and current condition remain relevant even below the count trigger.

The California internal claims-handling procedure requires prompt claim intake, recording of loss facts, verification of the policy and applicable coverages before coverage direction, mitigation within seven days after discovery under the Guide, evidence preservation, qualified investigation, documented communications, diary controls, and documented final disposition; these procedures do not decide coverage.

When HO 01 04 California Amendatory Endorsement is attached, its separate contract terms state claim acknowledgment within 15 days, a decision within 40 business days after requested items are received or a written explanation if unresolved, and payment of an accepted claim within 30 business days; these are form terms rather than appetite thresholds.

For the applicable CDI-2022-03 transaction position, the earthquake offer must be distinguished from the underlying homeowners policy, be written or electronic with consent, state material terms including a 15% seismic deductible, require affirmative acceptance before issuing the offered earthquake coverage, and retain delivery, response, and eligibility records; CDI-2014-06 remains relevant to policies written under its superseded position.

California referral and authority control requires clarification of missing information, referral of exceptions and unusual occupancy, construction, or loss concerns, aggregation of related interests rather than splitting to avoid referral, renewed review when material facts change before issuance, recorded approval before representing acceptance, and binding only after conditions and approved terms are confirmed.

The underwriting file must preserve the source and verification status of material facts, discrepancies and their resolution, eligibility and referral rationale, imposed conditions, authority level, communications, corrective-action evidence, and final disposition, including adverse information even when the risk is accepted.

California state-exception review adds pre-bind controls beyond routine Coverage A and protection-class eligibility, including verification of address and exterior condition, referral of unrepaired damage, open water or liability claims, incomplete construction, unsafe systems, foundation or drainage concerns, unusual occupancy, wildfire and access hazards, business or recreational exposures, unsupported safeguards or mitigation, and material changes before binding.

For California underwriting, replacement-cost settlement requires an insured-to-value review supporting 100%, and an unsupported or unreconciled replacement-cost estimate requires referral; this is an underwriting valuation control rather than a claim payment rule.

The California Guide's internal claims procedure extends beyond intake: before payment it requires cause, scope, estimate, valuation, deductible, limit, and replacement-cost review; it requires separating resulting damage from the source condition, handling proof-of-loss and additional-living-expense questions, preserving recovery rights, routing liability matters, documenting partial decisions, paying established undisputed amounts without waiting on unrelated disputes, and closing only after final disposition.

The current California earthquake-offer process requires a meaningful opportunity to consider the offer before the related transaction is completed, treats an information request as neither acceptance nor declination, requires filed and version-controlled offer materials and retained delivery and response records, and keeps the insurer responsible for producer, vendor, system, and translated-material implementations.

The California contract overlay states a 15% earthquake deductible based on applicable covered property value, while CDI-2022-03 requires the offer disclosure to state a 15% seismic deductible of applicable covered loss; underwriting must reconcile the issued contract, declarations, and filed offer rather than silently substituting one basis.

Before attaching earthquake-related coverage, underwriting must confirm that the attachment reflects California location and construction characteristics, review the quake deductible, and obtain authorized direction before altering, waiving, or negotiating that deductible.

The Personal Lines Manual's generic binding schedule is $800,000 for a line underwriter and $1,500,000 for a senior underwriter, while California Rule 520.A sets a $1,000,000 California line-underwriter ceiling; the handler's active assigned delegation remains controlling, these are carrier authority rules rather than policy limits, and a higher generic or senior level does not raise the California appetite ceiling.

Inspection-report timing is context-specific in the Manual: ordinary and renewal handling state 12 months after receipt or report date, endorsement attachment states 6 months, and Rule 610.AA says only “18 from its completion” without a unit; underwriting must record the dates and escalate the unclear 18-unit direction rather than inventing days, months, or another validity period.
